subject: Enquiry — does D153/1–8 contain a c.1875–1880 Llandough-juxta-Penarth instrument?
body:
Please would you check whether D153/1–8 contains any document dated c.1875–1880 relating to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth (ST 168 733), adjoining St Dochdwy’s churchyard. This is not Great House Farm, Llandough near Cowbridge.

I am looking for an agreement, lease, counterpart, award, conveyance or related plan involving any of: Daniel Thomas / D. Thomas & Son; Llandough Limeworks; John Williams / Thomas Williams; the Bute Estate or the Trustees of the Marquess of Bute; quarrying, minerals, lime, sidings, compensation or reparation; the dwelling adjoining the churchyard.

Also is there any item in D153/1–8 dated 1875–1880 naming Thomas Williams, John Williams, Daniel Thomas, Llandough Limeworks, or the dwelling by St Dochdwy’s?

Please confirm D/DRa 11/120 is Tynywain, Llanedeyrne, and not Llandough-juxta-Penarth/ Llandough Cardiff.

subject: RE: Enquiry — does D153/1–8 contain a c.1875–1880 Llandough-juxta-Penarth instrument?
body:
The majority of your email relates to document reference D153/1–8. As discussed in previous emails, this is a reference for material held at the National Library of Wales so you should contact them about these records. Detailed descriptions can be found on their online catalogue: Deeds relating to premises in p. Llandough, co. Glam., comprising a dwelling house adjoining the churchyard, 1811 (D153/1-2), land (19 ...

D/DRa 11/120 is an old way of formatting our reference DRA/11/120. This forms part of the series DRA/11/1-293 which comprises lawsuits, instructions to counsel, opinions etc. relating to undermining of house property, flooding, contravention of colliery regulations, 1856-1909 in respect of Elder’s Navigation Colliery, Maesteg. This doesn’t seem relevant to your research and doesn’t relate to Tynywain either. Can you point us to where you found this reference so that we can assist further?

subject: Re: Enquiry — does D153/1–8 contain a c.1875–1880 Llandough-juxta-Penarth instrument?
body: I note that D153/1–8 is held at the National Library of Wales and will pursue that route with them. I also note your clarification that DRA/11/120 (formerly D/DRa 11/120) relates to Elder’s Navigation Colliery, Maesteg, and is not relevant to Great House Farm / Ty Mawr, Llandough-juxta-Penarth. The reference originated from earlier research notes; I will not pursue it further with Glamorgan Archives.

subject: DBDT79/1 – physical examination of the original
body:
Request: physical examination of DBDT79/1. Catalogue entry: Lease (counterpart) of land and premises situate in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff, from the Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams, May 1877 [1 parchment, plan in margin].

1. Parties and date – Does the original name the Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams, and is it dated May 1877?

2. Property description – Exact wording of the land and premises. Does it expressly locate the property in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff?

3. Llandough / other references – Any mention (body text, plan, schedule, endorsements or annotations) of Llandough, Great House Farm / Tŷ Mawr, Western Ground Rents, or any locality outside Pembroke Terrace?

4. Marginal plan – Does the plan identify the location sufficiently?

5. Further identifying details – Any adjoining owners, plot numbers, parish, street numbers, measurements, previous ownership, rent, consideration, or cross-references to other instruments.

Catalogue wording discrepancy: most other 1877 entries in the series describe the grantor as the “Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute”. DBDT79/1 is catalogued simply as “from the Marquess of Bute”. From the original, please confirm who executed the lease and in what capacity.

subject: RE: DBDT79/1 – physical examination of the original
body:
The catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 had a few small errors which have now been corrected.

1. The document is a counterpart lease dated 2 May 1877 between the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute and Mr John Williams of Newport.

2. ‘All that piece or parcel of land with the messuage or tenement and outbuildings thereto now being erected and built or part thereof by the said lesee, situate, lying and being in Pembroke Terrace in the parish of St John the Baptist, Cardiff containing by admeasurement sixty-nine feet or thereabouts on the north side thereof, thirty-one feet or thereabouts on the east and west sides thereof and sixty-nine feet six inches or thereabouts on the south side thereof bounded on the north by land of the Marquess of Bute, on the east by Pembroke Terrace aforesaid, on the south by land demised to David Price and on the west by land of Mr John William Vachell.’

3. There is no mention of Llandough, Great House Farm or Ty Mawr or any other property outside of Pembroke Terrace.

4. The plan clearly shows a property on Pembroke Terrace. We can provide a digital copy at a charge of £15.60 (inclusive of VAT).

5. See above for full description. There is no further information included.
